subtopics.title: Three Ways to Measure One Economy

questions.question: The production, expenditure and income methods must give the same total because:
options: Everything produced is sold, everything sold is bought with someone's expenditure, and every rand of that expenditure becomes somebody's income
Statistics South Africa forces them to agree
They all measure only government activity
Intermediate goods are added in each method

questions.question: Flour bought by a bakery and flour bought by a household are classified differently because:
options: Bakery flour is a different product
Goods are classified by their USE, not their nature — bakery flour is intermediate, household flour is final

questions.question: The difference between a GROSS and a NET aggregate is:
options: Consumption of fixed capital — the wearing out of buildings and machines, which net totals subtract

questions.question: "Domestic" and "national" differ in that:
options: Domestic includes exports and national does not
Domestic is measured yearly and national quarterly
Domestic means inside the borders whoever owns the resources; national means earned by residents wherever the resources are

questions.question: Which list correctly gives the four classes of household consumption spending?
options: Durable, semi-durable, non-durable goods and services

questions.question: Durable purchases collapse first in a downturn because:
options: They are POSTPONABLE, while non-durables such as food are not

questions.question: Social grants are excluded from government final consumption expenditure (G) because:
options: They are too small to matter
They are paid by provinces, not by national government
They are TRANSFER payments — no good or service is bought in exchange, and the money is counted later inside C when the household spends it

questions.question: A new government-built hospital is recorded in:
options: G, because government paid for it
Neither, because it is free at the point of use
I — gross fixed capital formation — because it is capital spending, not day-to-day consumption

questions.question: Gross fixed capital formation is expenditure on:
options: Fixed assets used repeatedly in production for more than a year — buildings, construction works, machinery, transport equipment, ICT and cultivated assets
All goods bought by firms in a year
Raw materials and unsold stock only

questions.question: Buying an existing second-hand factory is NOT capital formation for the country because:
options: No NEW asset came into existence — only ownership moved
It is recorded as household consumption

questions.question: Gross fixed capital formation is R900 billion and consumption of fixed capital is R560 billion. NET investment is:
With GDP at R6 300 billion, investment of R900 billion represents about 14,3 per cent of GDP. Compared with the National Development Plan's target this is:
options: Not comparable, since the NDP sets no investment target
Well short — the NDP sets a target of roughly 30 per cent of GDP

subtopics.title: GVA, GNE and GNI — the Chain of Conversions

questions.question: C is 3 900, G is 1 400, I is 900 and the change in inventories is +50, all in rand billions. GNE is:
With GNE of 6 250, exports of 1 900 and imports of 1 850, GDP at market prices is:
To convert GVA at basic prices into GDP at market prices you:
options: Add taxes on products and subtract subsidies on products

questions.question: GDP is 6 300; primary income received from abroad is 90 and paid abroad is 240. GNI is:
options: R6 150 billion — structurally below GDP because more primary income leaves South Africa than enters it

questions.question: On the country's till slip, the household pile is:
options: C — the biggest pile, roughly three rand in every five
G — because government buys the most

questions.question: The taxi ride and the doctor's visit belong to which class of household spending?
options: Services — consumed as they are produced, leaving nothing behind

questions.question: Why is a social grant not counted in the government pile?
options: Because grants are paid in cash
Because government bought nothing with it — it is counted where the household spends it, and counting it twice would make the country look richer than it is
Because it is a form of tax

questions.question: "Furniture shops feel a downturn long before spaza shops do" because:
options: Furniture is taxed at a higher rate
The couch is postponable and food is not — durables fall first, non-durables hold steady

questions.question: Of R200 000 of stock, R80 000 of paint and a R400 000 delivery bakkie, the capital formation item is:
options: The bakkie — it is still there next year doing the work, rather than being used up

questions.question: A fruit orchard counts as fixed capital because:
options: The tree is used in production for many years — it is a machine that makes apples for twenty years

questions.question: A business spends R400 000 on a new bakkie while its old one suffers R150 000 of wear. Its real capacity improved by:
Investment matters more than the other spending piles because:
options: It is the only pile that makes NEXT year bigger — the production possibility curve stepping outward

questions.question: GNE is best described in plain words as:
options: The whole till slip added up — what the residents of this country SPENT
What South Africans keep after paying foreigners

questions.question: Spending R6 250 billion while producing R6 300 billion, with exports 1 900 and imports 1 850, shows that:
options: The gap between spending and production is settled through trade — and an economy that spends more than it produces runs a trade deficit

questions.question: GVA of 5 640 becomes GDP of 6 300 once you:
options: Add net primary income from abroad
Add R700 billion of taxes on products and subtract R40 billion of subsidies

questions.question: R6 150 billion rather than R6 300 billion "stays" because:
options: Government takes the difference in tax
Net primary income of R150 billion leaves the country — profit and interest earned here but paid to owners abroad
